label: weighted survey estimates, Afrobarometer Round 8 Tanzania 2021; components only, no composite

source.citation: Afrobarometer Data, Tanzania, Round 8, 2021, available at http://www.afrobarometer.org (form required by the Afrobarometer data usage and access policy, https://www.afrobarometer.org/data/data-usage-and-access-policy/)

estimation.weight_note: withinwt_hh: within-country weight to household level ('new AB withinwt'), adjusting for region, gender, urban-rural distribution and size of household, enumeration area and number of adults (codebook note); withinwt_ea (weights to EA level) is the alternative. Chosen because it includes household selection.
estimation.psu: INFERRED from identical region, urban/rural and EA_* items: 285 clusters (not a documented design)
estimation.interval: 95%, logit scale, Student-t, Taylor-linearised on the inferred design
estimation.bases: pct: respondents asked (don't know and refused stay in the base); pct_of_valid: substantive answers only

disclosure_rule: base < 10 suppressed; numerator < 10 withheld and the row flagged low_precision

composite.note: the 59.8% composite (assumed weights 30/35/20/15) is retired; the WVS 61.8% stays removed; only components are published

indicators.question: For each of the following actions, please tell me whether you think it is something a good citizen in a democracy should always do, never do, or do only if they choose: Good citizens should pay taxes they owe to the government (Tanzania-specific item Q76e-tan; wording from the Tanzania Round 8 codebook)
indicators.code_labels: 1=Never do, 2=Do only if they choose, 3=Always do, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Good citizens should ALWAYS pay the taxes they owe (civic duty to pay tax)

indicators.question: For each of the following statements, please tell me whether you disagree or agree: The tax authorities always have the right to make people pay taxes.
indicators.code_labels: 1=Strongly disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Agree, 5=Strongly agree, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Agree or strongly agree that the tax authorities always have the right to make people pay taxes

indicators.question: How much do you trust each of the following, or haven't you heard enough about them to say: The tax/revenue office?
indicators.code_labels: 0=Not at all, 1=Just a little, 2=Somewhat, 3=A lot, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know/Haven't heard
indicators.meaning: Trusts the tax/revenue office A LOT

indicators.question: How much do you trust each of the following, or haven't you heard enough about them to say: The tax/revenue office?
indicators.code_labels: 0=Not at all, 1=Just a little, 2=Somewhat, 3=A lot, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know/Haven't heard
indicators.meaning: Trusts the tax/revenue office somewhat or a lot

indicators.question: How many of the following people do you think are involved in corruption, or haven't you heard enough about them to say: Tax officials?
indicators.code_labels: 0=None, 1=Some of them, 2=Most of them, 3=All of them, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know/Haven't heard
indicators.meaning: Thinks most or all tax officials are involved in corruption (supporting indicator)

indicators.question: Q76e-tan, as above (Good citizens should pay taxes they owe to the government)
indicators.code_labels: 1=Never do, 2=Do only if they choose, 3=Always do, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Says good citizens should never pay, or pay only if they choose (does not hold paying tax to be a duty)

indicators.question: Not published in the codebook (the Tanzania Round 8 codebook carries a placeholder for Q80); the data-file variable label is 'Q80d_tan. Refused to pay a tax or fee' and the answer codes are those shown
indicators.code_labels: 0=No, would never do this, 1=No, would if had the chance, 2=Yes, once or twice, 3=Yes, several times, 4=Yes, often, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Has refused to pay a tax or fee (once or twice, several times or often)

indicators.question: Q80d_tan, as above (data-file label 'Refused to pay a tax or fee')
indicators.code_labels: 0=No, would never do this, 1=No, would if had the chance, 2=Yes, once or twice, 3=Yes, several times, 4=Yes, often, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Would never refuse to pay a tax or fee

indicators.question: In your opinion, how often, in this country, do people avoid paying the taxes that they owe the government?
indicators.meaning: Thinks people in this country often or always avoid paying the taxes they owe (perceived behaviour of others)

indicators.question: Do you agree or disagree with each of the following statements: The government usually uses the tax revenues it collects for the well-being of citizens.
indicators.code_labels: 1=Strongly disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Agree, 5=Strongly agree, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Agree or strongly agree that the government usually uses tax revenues for the well-being of citizens

indicators.question: How much of the time do you think the following try their best to listen to what people like you have to say: Members of Parliament?
indicators.meaning: Thinks Members of Parliament often or always try their best to listen to what people like them have to say

indicators.question: How much of the time do you think the following try their best to listen to what people like you have to say: Local government councilors?
indicators.meaning: Thinks local government councillors often or always try their best to listen to what people like them have to say

indicators.question: Now let us talk about the tax system in this country. Which of the following statements is closest to your view? Statement 1: It is better to pay higher taxes if it means that there will be more services provided by government. Statement 2: It is better to pay lower taxes, even if it means there will be fewer services provided by government.
indicators.code_labels: 1=Agree very strongly with Statement 1, 2=Agree with Statement 1, 3=Agree with Statement 2, 4=Agree very strongly with Statement 2, 5=Agree with neither, 8=Refused, 9=Don't know
indicators.meaning: Prefers paying higher taxes if that means more government services (supporting indicator)

indicators.question: Based on your experience, how easy or difficult is it to do each of the following: To find out what taxes and fees you are supposed to pay to the government?
indicators.meaning: Finds it difficult or very difficult to find out what taxes or fees one has to pay (supporting indicator; candidate for the 'simplicity' baseline, not mapped)

civic_duty_minus_reciprocity_gap.report_value: 28 pp (71% civic duty minus 43% 'government listens'; hand-typed from published figures, not reproducible from the file)

trust.score: weighted mean of the item rescaled to 0-1 ((code - 0) / 3), don't know / refused excluded
trust.mapping_rationale: Direct match: the driver is trust in the tax system; Q41J asks how much the respondent trusts the tax/revenue office.

social_norm.score: weighted mean of the item rescaled to 0-1 (1 - (code - 0) / 3, i.e. 1 = people never avoid paying tax), don't know / refused excluded
social_norm.mapping_rationale: The driver is the community norm of compliance; Q47D records how often people in the country avoid paying the taxes they owe, a descriptive norm (reversed so that 1 = others comply). The injunctive norm (Q76e-tan) is reported as a component but not used.

fairness.score: weighted mean of the item rescaled to 0-1 ((code - 1) / 4), don't know / refused excluded
fairness.mapping_rationale: The code's own gloss for the driver is 'perceived value for tax paid'; Q47C asks whether the government usually uses tax revenues for the well-being of citizens.

simplicity.label: information burden only (does not cover registration or filing costs)
simplicity.score: weighted mean of the item rescaled to 0-1 (1 - (code - 1) / 3, i.e. 1 = very easy to find out what taxes and fees to pay, 0 = very difficult), don't know / refused excluded
simplicity.mapping_rationale: Decision of the owner (Block E2.0): the simplicity driver is mapped to Afrobarometer Q46a (how easy or difficult it is to find out what taxes and fees you are supposed to pay to the government), reversed and rescaled 0-1. It measures the information burden only; it does not cover the cost of registering or filing, which the model's simplification interventions (USSD registration, presumptive tax) target.

enforcement.rationale: NOT MAPPED after the Block E2.1 search (kept as an ASSUMPTION for the owner's sign-off). Searched: the Afrobarometer Round 8 merged and Tanzania codebooks (every item mentioning tax with audit, penalty, punish, caught, enforce, detect, inspect, fine, prosecute, likely, evade, avoid: only Q47D 'how often do people avoid paying taxes' and, without the word tax, Q40G 'how often do ordinary people who break the law go unpunished' and Q40F 'officials who commit crimes go unpunished'); the FinScope 2023 data map (no item on audit, penalty or enforcement; the only tax item is the TIN document c27__13); the ILFS 2024 variable labels (no item on audit, inspection or penalty); TRA publications reachable on 2026-11-12 (Sixth Corporate Plan revised June 2024: KPI 'share of tax revenue from additional assessments raised in tax audits' 17.0% baseline, 14.5% actual 2022/23; no audit count, audit coverage rate or penalty amount; the TRA annual reports could not be located) and the NBS Tax Statistics Reports 2022/23 and 2023/24 (no audit data). Q40G is the closest survey item (perceived impunity of lawbreakers, general, reversed: unpunished -> weak enforcement) but it is not about tax; the audit-yield KPI is an outcome share of revenue, not a probability of being audited. Neither measures the perceived or actual likelihood of detection and penalty for not paying tax.
